author: ValWood
body:
Bip1, Scj1, Pdi4, Pdi5, Cnx1, and calreticulin are upstream of ERAD,  they're general ER protein-folding and quality-control machinery. They act on essentially all proteins passing through the ER (folding successfully or not), have no mechanism to commit a substrate to degradation, and continue functioning even for proteins that fold correctly and get secreted normally.

None of them is an ERAD component itself. The line into ERAD is crossed at:

Mns1 / Mnl1 — generate the ERAD-commitment signal (mannose trimming)

There are quite a lot of mappings or inferences for these:

bip1 GO:0036503 | ERAD pathway | IBA with locus:2182783 , PTN001834223 , S000003571
scj1 GO:0036503 | ERAD pathway | ISO with S000004827
pdi4 GO:0036503 | ERAD pathway | ISO with S000001267
pdi5 GO:0036503 | ERAD pathway | ISO with S000001267
cnx1 GO:0036503 | ERAD pathway | IBA with S000000054 , PTN000117401

@edwong57  these will probably need to move to a ER folding term,  can you see if you agreee? I used "protein folding in endoplasmic reticulum (GO:0034975)"    
 GO:0034975 should probably be moved under a general ER-quality control term,  but I'm not sure if everything annotated to this term is considered to be part of QC.   Otherwise, I will see if I can find an alternative "umbrella term" for the  2 parallell folding pathways that function as luminal proteins to enter the ER  (i.e., BiP/Hsp70 chaperone cycle and calnexin/calreticulin cycle.
